what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 2: Do massive records bound by a static possibility shift carry their binding energy as inertia?. LANDED FIRST: origin/main is the science authority; read each named note as landed (git show origin/main:docs/<note>) before any PR branch, and where a PR's wording differs from the landed text, the landed text controls. Blocks 115, 133, 139 and 142 are OPEN hand-off PRs (#9157, #9191, #9201, #9227): read them on their branches (gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName; git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>). Block 115 is a harvest of Grok-refereed attempts; blocks 139 and 142 are the supervisor's own derivations (Claude), NOT refereed by another family; nothing in them is adopted. SETTING: block 139 (PR #9201): the staggered mass m eps (eps = (-1)^{x1+x2+x3}) is the only site rest energy that keeps the books; a free massive walker has E^2 = sum sin^2 k + m^2, so at rest c^2 = d^2(E^2/2)/dk^2 = 1 along each axis (its inertia equals its rest energy). Block 133 (PR #9191): a massive body at rest sits on one sublattice, so two massive records at rest are never neighbours: a nearest-neighbour term binds them only through the other sublattice, and a two-step term (separation 2) binds them directly. Block 142 (PR #9227): compact pairs of massless records bound as neighbours are much heavier or lighter than their energy (c^2 = 1/2 on the line; no weight one along all axes in space). A supervisor exploration (floating point, NOT a result; the line, walkers sigma_z D + m eps, m = 4, one record per site, attraction V at separation 2, the pair's total momentum sector of the two-site translation) found the pair's weight W = E0 d^2E/dK^2 at rest to be 0.117, 0.201, 0.411 and 0.539 for V = -0.5, -0.3, -0.15 and -0.115; these fit W = 1/(4m|V|), which is block 142's half-line law for the pair on the massive records' own sublattice (relative hopping cos(K/2)/(4m)): W = 1 at the binding threshold |V| = 1/(4m), and near it 1 - W is of order (lattice spacing)/(pair size), a lattice effect of the pair's size. For two free relativistic bodies bound by a static potential U, expanding sqrt(m^2 + p^2) gives W = 1 + <U>/(2m) - <T>/m + ... (T the internal kinetic energy): a static binding's energy does not carry its share of inertia, and W falls short of one by about the binding fraction, however large the pair. The binding-fraction part is separate from the size part and does not shrink with the pair's size. TASK: (a) on the line and on Z^3, for two massive records under one record per site bound by a weak static two-step (or neighbour) term, compute the pair's weight exactly or with rigorous bounds as the pair loosens toward the binding threshold, and decide whether W - 1 approaches -(<T> - <U>/2)/m (the static formula) or 0; (b) separate the lattice part (the pair's size in lattice units) from the binding-fraction part; (c) decide whether any form of the binding term that depends on the pair's motion (for example on the records' two-step momenta or currents, or a term carried by the clock or the member) makes W = 1 at leading order in the binding fraction. HIT: (a) exact or rigorously bounded, or (c) settled. REGIME NOTE (added with refill p): on the lattice the pair's weight has a size part of order k^2 (k the constituents' wave number in lattice units) and a binding-fraction part of order T/m ~ k^2/m^2; the binding-fraction part dominates only when m << 1 in lattice units, the regime of masses far below the lattice scale, so study (a) and (b) there (the exploration at m = 4 measured the size part). DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/the-inertia-of-a-static-binding/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route.
